findings.title: Model and view state mutated without synchronization
findings.message: `selectMode` mutates `model.mode`, `view` and `g.Revision` from the button `Activate` callback. `model.prepare` reads `mode` and `view`, and writes `query`, `columns`, `sampleStart` and `sampleEnd`, from the canvas's Prepare path. The smoke goroutine likely reads the same fields. If the canvas prepares on a different goroutine than `Activate` runs on, these are unsynchronized shared accesses, and there is a torn-state risk between `mode` and `view`.
findings.suggestion: Protect the model and viewport with a mutex, or confirm in the driver contract that `Activate` and `Prepare` run on the same thread. Document that contract if so.

findings.title: Unsynchronized write to `status` from the smoke goroutine
findings.message: The `status` string is written from the smoke goroutine through this callback. It is also read by the window's `View` closure and written by `selectMode`, which likely run on the UI/driver thread. The code shows no synchronization, so this is a data race and will fail under `-race`. Unsynchronized string writes can also tear.
findings.suggestion: Guard `status` with a mutex or atomic.Value. Alternatively, run the status change on the UI thread through an app-provided dispatch function before calling `a.Invalidate("drawing")`.
findings.evidence: result <- drawingSmoke(ctx, a, g, other, model, nativeErrors, func() { status = "Chrome remains responsive" })

findings.title: Nil error dereference when receiving from nativeErrors
findings.message: If nativeErrors is closed, or a nil error is sent, the receive yields nil and err.Error() panics with a nil dereference instead of reporting a failed assertion. The same pattern appears later: `case err := <-nativeErrors: return err` would return nil and skip the success JSON event.
findings.suggestion: Use `case err, ok := <-nativeErrors:` and return a descriptive error when `!ok || err == nil`. Apply the same guard at the final non-blocking select.

findings.title: Native window resized outside the owner thread
findings.message: Every other access to window and canvas state in this smoke test goes through owner(), which runs on the application's owner thread. window.SetSize is called directly from the test goroutine. A native desktop window call from a non-owner thread can race or crash, and `go test -race` is part of the check script.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the call: `if err := owner(a, func() error { window.SetSize(size); return nil }); err != nil { return err }`.
